title: Materials and flows
about: The material conditions of a city and an economy: what a city's buildings weigh and of what they are made, with bounds that widen over what is not known of them; the flows that would renew the stock as its buildings age and are replaced; any stock over time from its inflows or its path; measured flows made to balance, with a test of whether they can; a product's life cycle; what an economy's final demand causes along its supply chains; and a community's greenhouse gas inventory by sector and scope, with measures against it credited so that two on one source are not both credited with what only one can save; and a city's solid waste from a household survey to what is managed in controlled facilities, with SDG 11.6.1 and its interval. The mathematics is the industrial-ecology domain's: dynamic stock models, material flow analysis and reconciliation, the matrix method of life cycle assessment, environmentally extended input–output analysis on economics' Leontief model, and the material stock of buildings, on calx's linear algebra and leading walks, tyche's laws and peira's survival.
